drhp.business: Advit Jewels manufactures 100% handmade fine jewellery - primarily Gold Kundan Meena Polki Jadau and cut-set diamond-with-Polki pieces (necklaces, earrings, rings, bangles and customized pieces) in 14- and 18-carat gold - from a single leased 6,450 sq ft unit in Jaipur that runs the full production cycle in-house. It sells predominantly B2B to dealers, showrooms and jewellery retailers, with a smaller B2C made-to-order business, and is setting up a flagship store in Jaipur. The 'Rambhajo' brand traces to a jewellery business established in 1921.

objects_execution.note: SME all-fresh-issue. Working-capital requirement of Rs 6,500 lakhs to fund gold/stone procurement, finished inventory and trade receivables (fund-based WC facilities were Rs 5,408.89 lakhs at Dec 31, 2025). GCP capped at 25% of Gross Proceeds; the Rs 2,290 lakhs Pre-IPO placement is earmarked for GCP. No plant/machinery capex or defined deployment/capex project exists - Objects are working capital + debt repayment + GCP only, so project fields are structural/null. Net Proceeds deployment is scheduled across FY2026-27 (WC Rs 5,500 L + debt repayment Rs 6,500 L) and FY2027-28 (WC Rs 1,000 L), with any unutilised balance carried to FY2028-29. Per Means of Finance, all Objects are funded entirely from the Net Proceeds and net worth / internal accruals (no debt component); no firm-arrangement requirement under Reg 7(1)(e). The 7-storey Jaipur retail store and franchise rollout are stated growth initiatives, not issue-funded capex objects.

concerns_observed: Persistent negative operating cash flows: Rs -277.25 (FY23), Rs -1,049.33 (FY24) and Rs -3,697.69 lakhs (FY25), driven by a working-capital-intensive B2B credit model, despite strong reported profits.
Inventory build-up: inventory rose from Rs 1,041.67 lakhs (FY23) to Rs 4,491.67 lakhs (FY25) with inventory holding days of 199 (FY25) vs 91 (FY23).
Customer and channel concentration: top customers were 94.90% / 88.08% of revenue and B2B was 82.60% / 81.63% across recent periods, on flexible credit terms.
Raw-material (gold/diamond polki) dependence: raw materials are ~99.85% of cost of materials consumed, procured spot with no long-term contracts, so gold-price spikes compress margins.
Single leased manufacturing facility in Jaipur with capacity under-utilisation (45.86% in FY25) and geographic concentration (Rajasthan-led).
Rising leverage (debt-to-equity 0.32 FY23 -> 0.60 FY24 and higher; secured borrowings of Rs 8,163.93 lakhs sanctioned by May 2026) backed by promoter personal/corporate guarantees.

Governance: 2 of 4 promoters (incl. a 20-year-old) lack business experience; most directors lack listed-company experience; past discrepancies in RoC filings; a 3200:1 bonus issue shortly before the IPO with promoter average cost of acquisition of Nil.
Promoters/directors carry litigation aggregating ~Rs 340.04 lakhs (largely a promoter personal property/title dispute), and jewellery designs are not registered under the Designs Act, 2000.

red_flags: 3200:1 bonus issue on August 26, 2025 shortly before the IPO, with promoter average cost of acquisition of Nil.
Negative operating cash flow in FY23-FY25 even as revenue nearly tripled - profits not converting to cash due to inventory/receivables build.
Past discrepancies in filings with the Registrar of Companies and other non-compliances, plus delays in employee statutory dues.
Secured borrowings backed by promoter personal and corporate guarantees, with rising debt-to-equity.
A 20-year-old promoter director and several promoters engaged in numerous other (real-estate) businesses/LLPs.
strengths_observed: Strong revenue growth with high margins: revenue from operations rose from Rs 4,660.41 lakhs (FY23) to Rs 6,944.26 lakhs (FY24) to Rs 12,493.73 lakhs (FY25), with EBITDA margin ~27-30% and PAT margin ~20-22% throughout.
High capital efficiency: FY25 RoE 55.79%, RoNW 43.64% and RoCE 27.48%; RoNW has been above 43% across FY23-FY25.
Volume growth of 38.92% in Fiscal 2025 versus Fiscal 2023 despite rising gold prices, indicating real (not just price-led) demand.
100+ year 'Rambhajo since 1921' brand heritage and a promoter family with 26+ years of jewellery experience.
In-house, single-roof manufacturing (melting to finishing) enabling design customization, quality control, shorter lead times (25-30 days) and cost/security control.
Net worth grew from Rs 1,807.82 lakhs (FY23) to Rs 8,365.16 lakhs (Dec 31, 2025); operating cash flow turned positive (Rs 1,782.96 lakhs) in 9M FY26.

sk.overview: India's gems and jewellery retail industry - covering gold jewellery, studded (diamond/coloured stone) jewellery and other (silver/platinum) jewellery plus gold bars and coins - was estimated at Rs 12,887 billion in fiscal 2026 and forms about 8.3% of India's overall retail market. Demand is culturally anchored in weddings, festivals, births and the harvest season, and gold doubles as a savings asset, particularly in rural India.
